<p class="eyebrow">Research</p>
<h1 class="page-title">Research</h1>
<p class="page-lede">My primary doctoral interest is how infrastructure-finance arrangements distribute fiscal and foreign-exchange risk and decision-making authority in lower-income economies. I am developing a public-source study of Malawi’s energy sector.</p>
</div>
</header>

<section id="doctoral-project" class="section-block" aria-labelledby="doctoral-project-title">
<div class="site-shell">
<div class="project-heading">
<div>
<p class="project-kicker">Proposed doctoral project · feasibility and design stage</p>
<h2 id="doctoral-project-title">Public Risk, Private Control?</h2>
</div>
<p class="project-summary">When governments and development institutions guarantee privately financed infrastructure, do they gain meaningful control over investment and service provision, or mainly assume fiscal and foreign-exchange risk?</p>
</div>

<div class="project-body">
<div>
<h3>Why Malawi’s energy sector?</h3>
<p>Malawi combines acute foreign-exchange and debt constraints with a visible mix of private, public, and multilateral financing arrangements. That makes it possible to study how macroeconomic constraints are translated into project contracts, guarantees, payment obligations, and ownership structures.</p>
<p>A first public-source audit has identified three initial cases: the operational Salima and Golomoti solar projects and the proposed Mpatamanga storage-hydropower project. A closer public or locally financed comparator will enter the study only if comparable records can be recovered.</p>
</div>
<div>
<h3>Current design</h3>
<ul class="project-list">
<li>Keep announced, approved, financed, constructed, and operational stages distinct.</li>
<li>Reconstruct financing layers, guarantees, currency exposure, ownership, and decision rights from official and project records.</li>
<li>Code common fields for public exposure, investor protections, reciprocal obligations, project status, and documented service outcomes.</li>
<li>Test the interpretation against domestic-capacity, technology, project-selection, and policy-error explanations.</li>
</ul>
<p class="evidence-limit"><strong>Current evidence limit:</strong> the design supports transaction reconstruction and comparative process analysis. It does not yet identify an average causal effect of public versus private finance.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</section>

<span class="status-tag">Co-authored methods paper · April 2022</span>
<h3>Robust Inference in the Presence of Weak Instruments</h3>
<p class="work-meta">With Kartika Herscheid and Unai Oyón-Lerga · Paris School of Economics</p>
<p>A retrospective reassessment of 437 just-identified IV specifications from 38 <em>American Economic Journal</em> papers, applying the tF robust-inference adjustment. The exercise documents how the adjustment changes reported inference; it does not re-estimate the original studies.</p>

<section id="ai-interest" class="section-block" aria-labelledby="ai-interest-title">
<div class="site-shell narrow-section">
<p class="project-kicker">Developing research interest</p>
<h2 id="ai-interest-title">AI adoption, firms, and work</h2>
<p>I am interested in which firms adopt AI in lower-income economies, which organisational and technical capabilities shape use, and whether adoption changes tasks, monitoring, and worker discretion.</p>
<p>One feasibility route uses World Bank Enterprise Survey AI follow-ups to measure reported adoption across firm size, exporting, foreign ownership, skills, and prior digital capacity. The immediate goal is descriptive measurement. A causal design would require credible adoption timing, observed use, defensible comparison groups, and adequate follow-up data.</p>
<p>This is an early research direction, not a completed independent paper.</p>
</div>
</section>

<section class="section-block ruled-section" aria-labelledby="software-title">
<div class="site-shell">
<div class="section-intro compact-intro">
<div>
<p class="eyebrow">Open-source work</p>
<h2 id="software-title">Research software and replications</h2>
</div>
<div class="intro-copy software-list">
<p><a href="https://github.com/mkmacho/ai-qualitative-interviews"><strong>AI qualitative interviews</strong></a> — an open-source, Qualtrics-integrated application for structured long-form qualitative data collection using language models. It supports configurable interviews and validation; research protocols, consent, data protection, and human oversight remain the responsibility of the research team.</p>
<p><a href="https://github.com/mkmacho/newslabor-extract"><strong>Newspaper labour extraction</strong></a> — reproducible Python and SLURM pipelines for OCR-derived historical job advertisements.</p>
<p><a href="https://github.com/mkmacho/llm-experimental-economics-simulation"><strong>LLM Experimental Economics Simulation</strong></a> — a code-only framework that reconstructs an experimental-economics design from public materials and evaluates heuristic or LLM agents against empirical targets. It documents leakage safeguards and reproducible simulation audits; results are not yet presented as empirical findings.</p>
<p><a href="https://github.com/mkmacho/colombia-education-cct-replication"><strong>Colombia education CCT replication</strong></a> — a reproducible R baseline replication of treatment effects from Barrera-Osorio et al.’s Colombian conditional cash-transfer experiment, using the authors’ official replication package.</p>
<p><a href="https://github.com/mkmacho/basel-transit-investment-analysis"><strong>Basel transit investment analysis</strong></a> — a reproducible spatial-analysis portfolio project combining Swiss GTFS and Basel-Stadt open data with a locally authorised business-location input. Its grant and investment scenario is fictional: it demonstrates geocoding, spatial joins, transit-access metrics, validation, and map/report outputs, not an evaluation or policy recommendation.</p>
<p><a href="https://github.com/mkmacho/constrained-slate-recommender"><strong>Constrained slate recommender</strong></a> — an independent synthetic-data reference implementation of a constrained recommender. It grew out of earlier work at ConsiliumBots on <em>Decidiendo para un Futuro Mejor</em> (DFM), conducted with J-PAL LAC; it contains no partner data, code, or configuration and is not a release of the DFM system.</p>
</div>
